readingInstruction: Read Isaiah 40:1-42:25. The second half of Isaiah begins here. The mood shifts from judgment to comfort. Read chapter 40 slowly, and listen for the voice crying in the wilderness.
settingTheScene: Isaiah 40 opens the second half of the book. Chapters 40 to 55 speak to a people who, in the prophet’s vision, are in exile in Babylon, as Isaiah 39 foretold. The message is “Comfort, comfort my people.” God is going to bring them back. These chapters present the incomparable God, his Servant, and his plan to redeem. They are some of the most beautiful and doctrinally rich in the Old Testament.
observation: “Comfort, comfort my people, says your God. Speak tenderly to Jerusalem” (40:1-2).
“A voice cries: In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD” (40:3).
“The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever” (40:8).
“Behold your God! … He will tend his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms” (40:9, 11).
“To whom then will you compare me, that I should be like him? says the Holy One” (40:25).
“They who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles” (40:31).
“Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations” (42:1).
“A bruised reed he will not break, and a faintly burning wick he will not quench” (42:3).
interpretation:
Isaiah 40 begins with a double command: “Comfort, comfort my people.” After the long section of judgment, God speaks tenderly. The warfare is ended, the iniquity pardoned. The people have received double for their sins, which means that their punishment is complete. A voice cries out for a highway to be built for the LORD in the wilderness. This is the announcement of God’s own return to his people.

The chapter next deals with the reasons for trust. First, God’s word stands forever, though human strength is like grass. Second, God is a shepherd who carries the lambs in his arms and gently leads those that are with young. Third, God is incomparable. He measured the waters in the hollow of his hand. The nations are like a drop from a bucket. The idols are made by craftsmen who nail them in place so they do not fall. Those who sit in exile feel forgotten, but God never grows weary. He gives power to the faint and strengthens the weak. Those who wait for him renew their strength.

Chapter 41 continues with God’s courtroom challenge to the idols and the nations. “Fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God.” To Israel, called “worm Jacob,” he says that he is their redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.

Then in chapter 42 appears the first of the Servant Songs. “Behold my servant.” He is chosen, upheld, and endowed with God’s Spirit. His mission is to bring justice to the nations, not with a loud voice but with gentleness. “A bruised reed he will not break.” The Servant does not crush the weak. He will not grow faint or be discouraged until he has established justice in the earth. And the coastlands wait for his law.

The Servant is a mystery in Isaiah, and the question of who he is will keep returning. In this song, he is presented as the one who will bring God’s justice, with compassion for the weak.
connection: All four Gospels apply Isaiah 40:3 to John the Baptist (Matthew 3:3; Mark 1:2-3; Luke 3:4-6; John 1:23). Matthew 12:15-21 quotes Isaiah 42:1-4 and applies it to Jesus. At his baptism, the Father’s voice echoed this, “my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:17). 1 Peter 1:24-25 quotes Isaiah 40:6-8. John 10:11 shows Jesus as the good shepherd. Matthew 11:28-30 reveals his gentleness.
application:
Memorize Isaiah 40:31, and apply it to an area where you are weary.

Think of someone who feels like a bruised reed. Be gentle with them this week.

Spend time meditating on the greatness of God in Isaiah 40:12-26, and let it shrink your problems.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to comfort his people, including you.
Ask him to prepare the way in your heart.
Thank him for the shepherd who carries the lambs.
